processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr (x=0) steel strips were prepared by centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification in an argon atmosphere; the molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm to give as-cast strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. This is the parent (as-cast) state of the annealed 0Cr sample. Near-rapid solidification gives a cooling rate of 1–1 × 10^4 K/s.

Some as-cast steel strips (including the 0Cr strip) were annealed at 600 °C for 3 h in a tubular vacuum furnace, referred to as 'annealed steel strips'. This treatment promotes precipitation of κ-carbides without coarsening, giving better comprehensive mechanical properties.

structures.overall_structure: γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed in it; nano-scale κ-carbides precipitated in the γ-austenite and ordered DO3 phase in the δ-ferrite. Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h increases δ-ferrite volume fraction (to 6%) and promotes the precipitation and growth of κ-carbides; the double peak (110)δ/(220)DO3 between 43.5° and 45.0° collapses to a single peak indicating almost all ferrite transforms into ordered DO3 phase.

precipitates.distribution: distributed in γ-austenite; a large number of nano-scale κ-carbides in the annealed 0Cr steel strip

microstructure_list.region: irregular δ-ferrite distributed in γ-austenite matrix

phases_present.morphology: irregularly shaped, short rod-like and branched ferrite

precipitates.distribution: in the δ-ferrite (ordered phase occupying the ferrite; upon annealing almost all ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation entanglement at the γ-austenite/δ-ferrite phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation entanglements occur at the phase boundary between ferrite and austenite, attributed to the inconsistent deformation of ferrite and austenite during deformation (observed in the annealed 0Cr/6Cr strips after tensile deformation).

interfaces.slip_behavior: In the annealed 0Cr strip at a true strain of 0.075, {111} planar slip bands and dislocation arrays are present in the austenite, indicating a typical planar slip characteristic; a typical dislocation network structure is also present. At the final strain stage a large number of slip bands and many microbands appear; slip bands can extend through a grain boundary producing small steps (a low-angle grain boundary with misorientation 2.56°). A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism acts at early and final strain stages respectively.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h makes the double peak (110)δ/(220)DO3 between 43.5° and 45.0° change into a single peak, indicating almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase; the δ-ferrite volume fraction of the 0Cr strip increases from 3% (as-cast) to 6% on annealing.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm and gage length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile tests performed at least 3 times

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the annealed 0Cr strip is given in Fig. 3(b); the 0Cr curve reaches the highest plateau stress at the lowest strain and fractures earliest (~28% strain).
strain_hardening_rate: annealed 0Cr strip shows a clear double-hump strain hardening rate feature (Fig. 3(d)); its strain hardening rate is lower than that of the corresponding as-cast strip; the first hump is related to slip-band refinement and the second to microband formation

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength: annealing at 600 °C for 3 h increased the yield strength of the 0Cr steel strip by 131 MPa (as-cast 836 MPa → annealed 967 MPa)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning angle 30°–100°, continuous scanning at a speed of 4°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase characterization of the as-cast and annealed low-density steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: The annealed 0Cr strip consists mainly of austenite and ferrite; the double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° in the as-cast strip changes into a single peak upon annealing, indicating that almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: after mechanical polishing and etching; etching solution 3.3 vol% nitric acid, 3.3 vol% acetic acid and 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid, etching time 3 s; photographs taken at a position 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure and phase fraction determination of the δ-ferrite
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix; the volume fraction of δ-ferrite in the annealed 0Cr steel strip is 6% (increased from 3% as-cast).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V with a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF/DF imaging and SADP along [110] zone axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate nano-scale precipitated phases (κ-carbides, DO3) in γ-austenite and δ-ferrite
characterization_methods.key_findings: DF (001) images show a large number of nano-scale κ-carbides in the annealed 0Cr strip; the measured volume fraction and average size of the κ-carbides are 7% and 8 nm, respectively.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the average density of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: The measured average density of the 0Cr steel strip is 6.71 g/cm³.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and CS2800 carbon-sulfur analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the compositions of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured composition of the 0Cr steel (wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal. (Table 1).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, constant strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1, per GB/T-228.1-2010, gage width 4 mm and gage length 12 mm, at least 3 tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 0Cr strip: YS 967 ± 28 MPa, UTS 1016 ± 22 MPa, TE 30 ± 1 % (Table 2).

unmapped_findings: Annealing the 0Cr strip at 600 °C for 3 h increased the δ-ferrite volume fraction from 3% (as-cast) to 6% (annealed).
The annealing treatment (600 °C, 3 h) increased the yield strength of the 0Cr steel strip by 131 MPa (from as-cast 836 ± 7 MPa to annealed 967 ± 28 MPa).
The UTS × TE product of the annealed 0Cr steel strip is 30.5 GPa% (UTS 1016 MPa × TE 30%).
Measured composition of the 0Cr steel strip (wt.%, Table 1): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal.
Measured density of the 0Cr steel strip is 6.71 g/cm³ (vs 6.69 g/cm³ for 3Cr and 6.66 g/cm³ for 6Cr).

The annealed 0Cr strip exhibits a clear double-hump-like feature in its strain hardening rate curve (Fig. 3(d)); the first hump is related to slip-band refinement and the second to the formation of microbands, with the number of nano-scale κ-carbides playing a crucial role at the early strain stage.

For the annealed 0Cr strip at a true strain of 0.075 during tensile deformation, {111} planar slip bands and dislocation arrays are present in the austenite (typical planar slip), and a typical dislocation network structure is also present in the austenite.

After tensile fracture the true strains of the annealed 0Cr and 6Cr steel strips are 0.255 and 0.298, respectively; many microbands (marked with white arrows) appear in the austenite matrix in addition to slip bands, and the microstructures of the two strips are similar after fracture.

In the annealed 0Cr (and 6Cr) strip the slip bands can extend through a grain boundary producing many small steps; the SADPs on both sides indicate a low-angle grain boundary with a misorientation of 2.56° (observed only at high strain).

A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening of the low-density steel strips: slip-band hardening acts at the early strain stage and microband hardening at the final strain stage.
Shared annealing treatment: the same 600 °C/3 h annealing in a tubular vacuum furnace was applied to all three alloy compositions (0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr).

Data reported for the as-cast 0Cr sibling (not the annealed sample): κ-carbide measured volume fraction and average size 3% and 6 nm; measured lattice parameter of κ-carbide 0.387 nm and γ-austenite 0.375 nm; DO3 phase in δ-ferrite with size 26 ± 3 nm.
